newsitem.title: CHINA: RTRS - Qantas inaugurates Sydney-Shanghai flights.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Qantas inaugurates Sydney-Shanghai flights.

text.p: The Australian airline Qantas Airways Ltd on Wednesday inaugurated flights to Shanghai, adding the city to its twice-weekly run between Sydney and Beijing, and an official said he saw huge growth potential for the route.

Qantas' Group Executive General Manager Commercial Geoff Dixon said in an interview that the airline was making money on the China route, which opened in March last year, with load factors of around 80 percent.
But he said he expected load factors to decline as extra capacity entered the route, with China Eastern airlines and Ansett scheduled to start services before the end of this year.
Dixon said Qantas planned to expand its China flights to four a week from around April next year, particularly to take advantage of a hoped-for expansion in tourist travel.
"We don't see it as a goldmine, particularly in the short term, but there's a lot going for it in terms of the business markets and the tourist market from both Australia and China," Dixon said.
He said Australia hoped it would be designated as an approved tourist destination for China's growing number of tour groups travelling abroad.
"I think the time is ripe now for airlines like Qantas to establish themselves in China whereas five years ago it would have been too early," Dixon said.
He said heavy discounting of tickets on the route was a problem, with an economy Shanghai-Sydney ticket of 20,000 yuan selling in the market for up to half that.
British Airways has 25 percent of Qantas.
